title: Surface Variables Description of Axion Topological Materials
abstract: We study the response of axion topological materials under the presence of external static electric and magnetic fields. We focus on the macroscopic quasi-static magnetoelectric response of topological insulators. We use techniques based on surface variables that have been previously employed in soft condensed matter problems for the description of heterogeneous systems composed of multiple homogeneous materials. A complete description of the whole system is written in terms of surface degrees of freedom, which in this case correspond to effective surface charge and surface current densities. We obtain a set of integral equations satisfied by these variables. We present exact analytic solutions for axial-symmetric cases. We develop a numerical method for the solution of the integral equations by means of a boundary finite element method. We apply the numerical method to topological insulators with different geometries such as spheres, hollow spheres and toroidal surfaces. We show that that a variational principle can be used to recover the surface variables equations.
summary: This paper develops a powerful theoretical framework to analyze how axion topological insulators respond to external electric and magnetic fields. By reformulating the problem using 'surface variables' instead of bulk descriptions, the authors derive solvable integral equations for induced surface charges and currents. This method allows for detailed numerical simulations on complex geometries like spheres and tori.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the macroscopic quasi-static magnetoelectric response of axion topological materials, specifically topological insulators, when subjected to external static electric and magnetic fields.
main_result: The authors derive a set of integral equations governing effective surface charge and current densities, providing exact analytic solutions for axial-symmetric cases and developing a boundary finite element method for complex geometries.
method: The core methodology involves reformulating the bulk field equations using 'surface variables' (effective surface charge/current), leading to linear integral equations that are solved numerically via a boundary finite element approach.

important_parameters: Quasi-static regime, external static E and B fields, geometry (spheres, tori).

The analysis assumes a quasi-static limit and treats $

paper_structure: The paper follows a logical progression: establishing the Hamiltonian formulation, introducing surface variables to derive integral equations, presenting analytic solutions for simple cases, detailing the numerical boundary finite element method, and finally applying this framework to complex geometries.
why_interesting: While not directly focused on quantum information, the rigorous mathematical treatment of topological responses using reduced-dimensionality surface variable methods is highly relevant to modern condensed matter theory dealing with emergent electromagnetic properties in novel materials.
